title: Which numbers are ready for the board?
prompt:
Create a large 16:9 landscape infographic for a general professional audience (managers, engineers new to the topic, students), light near-white background, warm and clear like a well-designed museum explainer or a quality newspaper graphic. Plain everyday language is the main text; technical names appear only as small grey secondary labels.

TITLE (large): "Which numbers are ready for the board?"
SUBTITLE: "TOKN reviewed six energy and carbon analyses and released only what was properly sourced and disclosed."

BAND 1 — heading "Why this matters": one wide card with a simple flat illustration of a boardroom report with an energy chart and a wind turbine, and this text: "Board packs drive investments and public climate claims. An unsourced figure or an unstated assumption can mislead a decision worth millions."

BAND 2 — heading "Who did the work": a left-to-right flow of eight round role badges joined by arrows. Each badge shows a line icon, the bold role name, the short description in quotes, and the model name tiny and grey below:
1 Scout — "lists the tools available" (claude-haiku-5.5) [icon: binoculars]
2 Planner — "writes what 'done' looks like" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: document]
3 Analyst — "runs the official checks" (Kimi-K3.1-Pro) [icon: bar chart]
4 Skeptic — "re-checks and finds 10 weak spots" (FW-GLM-5.3) [icon: shield]
5 Judge — "decides: revise or ship?" (Microsoft-Decision-1) [icon: balance scale]
6 Editor — "fixes every weak spot" (gpt-6.1-sol) [icon: pencil]
7 Coach — "writes a lesson for next time" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: lightbulb]
8 Examiner — "scores it with plain code, no AI" (verify.py) [icon: checklist]
Caption under the flow: "Like a newsroom: a writer, a fact-checker, an editor — and an exam nobody can sweet-talk."

BAND 3 — heading "Four questions every analysis must answer": four cards in a row, each with an icon, the question in large plain words, and a tiny grey tool label:
(database icon) "Where did the data come from?" — tiny grey label: validate_data_provenance
(sliders icon) "Are the scenario assumptions disclosed?" — tiny grey label: enforce_scenario_disclosure
(warning triangle icon) "Is the market language careful?" — tiny grey label: enforce_market_disclaimer
(factory inside a dashed boundary icon) "Is the carbon boundary stated?" — tiny grey label: enforce_carbon_boundary

BAND 4 — heading "What it found": 6 result cards in a row. Each shows the small ID at top, a large verdict word in its color with a matching status icon, and one plain sentence:
EN-1 — green (#16A34A) verdict "Release" — "Energy balance from metered data."
EN-2 — red (#DC2626) verdict "Held back" — "Capacity scenario has no discount rate."
EN-3 — red (#DC2626) verdict "Held back" — "Power-purchase valuation called itself 'risk-free'."
EN-4 — red (#DC2626) verdict "Held back" — "Carbon inventory doesn't say where its data came from."
EN-5 — amber (#D97706) verdict "Release with caveat" — "A modelled projection, labelled as one."
EN-6 — green (#16A34A) verdict "Release" — "Demand forecast, labelled as estimated."
Small note at the right of the heading: "2 released · 1 with a caveat · 3 held back."

BOTTOM BAND — three short panels:
"Trust, but verify" — "An independent checker re-ran the checks and plain code graded the result: 6 of 6 correct."
"Honest wording" — "Projections are labelled as projections, and confidence is capped by data quality."
"Getting better each run" — "The lesson saved for next time: Submit inputs exactly as stored; never from a redacted display."

FOOTER (small, centered): "The takeaway: 'Risk-free' is two words that can cost a board its credibility."

TEXT DISCIPLINE: use ONLY the words given above in quotes plus the headings. Do NOT add any slogans, taglines, mottos, handwritten notes, brand lines, decorative words, extra footers or invented statistics. Every word spelled exactly as given and legible at 4K.

Visual rules: generous whitespace, strong hierarchy (title > band headings > plain sentences > tiny grey technical labels), verdict colors only on the result cards, soft blue/teal section tints, flat friendly line icons. No people, no faces, no photos.
